source.title: A Generalisation Signal Need Not Be a Model-Selection Signal
source.authors: Aditya Nagarsekar; M. P. Ashish Bhat; Aadi Nesarkar; Vrishti Godhwani; Rahul Yedida; Aditya Challa; Danda Sravan; Snehanshu Saha

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether training-set geometry tracks generalisation gap and helps model selection under biological distribution shifts. It refines the broader claim: gap correlation does not ensure useful model selection, and collapse can make low geometric scores misleading. It does not test the specific magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7.
record.gate_note: Results from prior studies are cited but not extracted. The paper's own experiments measure its activation proxy and full-network curvature; the proxy is not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure named in V7.
record.test_reason: The study measures activation energy, full-network Hessian summaries, and model-selection performance in biological regression. It does not measure V7's magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance or compare its gap rankings with norm- and margin-based measures. Its own results test none of V1–V8; citing Jiang et al. and finding failures of other geometric measures does not establish a test of V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Training-set signals can contain generalization information without consistently improving deployment-model selection; outcomes depend on the task and selection rule, and low scores can reward collapsed predictors. The authors restrict this conclusion to the tested models, representations, selection rules, and geometric criteria.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains ReLU MLPs with Adam and coupled L2, then measures an activation proxy and full-network curvature and tests selection under biological distribution shift; it does not reproduce any listed original intervention or measure.
record.method_sensitivity: The proxy-gap association changes by dataset and can reverse or approach zero. Selection outcomes also vary by shift; on Amylase the apparent proxy gain is a collapse artifact, while on Hydrophobic Core proxy-augmented validation harms performance.

fits_no_version.finding: The activation proxy's partial gap correlations range from +0.16 to +0.56 on molecular tasks and Amylase, but are −0.30 on Hydrophobic Core and +0.01 on GDSC2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-energy proxies can carry task-dependent generalization-gap information in biological regression.

fits_no_version.finding: Unscaled Hessian summaries have weak or negative gap associations. The norm-weighted trace correlates positively on two molecular conditions and negatively on Hydrophobic Core; controlling for weight norm largely removes the molecular trace association.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Full-network curvature and approximate relative flatness have condition-dependent associations with generalization gaps in these MLP regressors.

fits_no_version.finding: On audited Hydrophobic Core pools, proxy-only selection has no significant MSE advantage over validation, while validation augmented with the proxy significantly worsens MSE.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A training-set geometric signal need not improve deployment-model selection under biological shift.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026 workshop: I Can’t Believe It’s Not Better (ICBINB): Failure Modes of AI in Biology
record.problems: The experiments are limited to supervised regression with ReLU MLPs and fixed representations. Candidates train for a fixed 100 epochs and are not all converged. The degeneracy audit is post-hoc. GDSC2 and several analyses are exploratory or added after unblinding. The authors state that tested selection rules do not include combining geometry with training loss or allowing the signal direction to vary by condition.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported task-level model-selection results beyond the Hydrophobic Core outcomes were extracted; the paper reports compressed aggregates or extensive per-condition tables for other conditions, but those are not needed to represent the gap-correlation findings and the reversal. No values used only to choose hyperparameters or cited prior-work results are rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance performance on random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond zero training error under converged, unregularized training.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Controlled dropout effects on held-out classifier error. Sampling dropout in a multivariate search does not establish this effect.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance, its association with gaps among similarly well-fitted convolutional networks, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the reader's tests/T5 classification: failures of these alternative geometric measures do not challenge the specifically defined V7. No omitted result directly tests a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalisation coexistence.
Test error across widths beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.measure: Partial correlations for λmax, tr(H), ∥w∥² tr(H), ∥w∥² alone, Proxy, and tr(H) given ∥w∥²
rows.note: These are full-network quantities; the authors state they did not measure the final-layer Hessian separately.
rows.check: Values match Table 20, but this bundles three conditions and six measures. The norm-weighted trace is explicitly an approximate relative-flatness surrogate, not V7's perturbation-tolerance measure. Hutchinson relative standard errors quantify trace estimation, not correlation uncertainty.
